title: Modeling Personality Traits by Predicting Questionnaire Responses as an Alternative Approach to Filipino Automatic Personality Recognition
authors: Gomez, A. P. I.; Kahil, I. D.; Ong, S. V. N.; Tighe, E. P.
tldr: Explores Filipino APR by predicting individual BFI questionnaire responses from Twitter text, then aggregating to estimate Extraversion and Conscientiousness trait scores.
problem_and_motivation: Direct personality trait modeling from social media text yields subpar results. An alternative item-based approach predicting individual questionnaire responses may improve accuracy but requires validation.
approach: Used PagkataoKo dataset of 2,168 Filipino X (formerly Twitter) users with BFI responses.
Trained logistic regression, SVM, and XGBoost models on TF-IDF and term occurrence features.
Predicted individual BFI item responses for Extraversion and Conscientiousness.
Aggregated item predictions to estimate overall trait scores.
Experimental parameters included n-gram range, feature reduction (chi-square, PCA), and model configurations.
findings: Item-level prediction shows some improvement over direct trait modeling for Conscientiousness.
Overall trait-level performance remains lacking for both Extraversion and Conscientiousness.
Hierarchical classification scheme improved Conscientiousness prediction.
Significant improvements needed before item-based framework is viable for APR.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Explores item-response prediction as alternative to direct trait modeling for APR. Provides benchmark results for Filipino personality recognition using social media text. Identifies performance gaps requiring future improvement.
directly_justifies: Item-level prediction approach shows limited improvement for Filipino APR.
Conscientiousness sees better results than Extraversion with hierarchical approach.
limits: Limited to two BFI dimensions; other personality traits not explored.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 5.C medium for classification methodology. Rejected financial topics as paper focuses on personality recognition, not finance.

limitations: Model performance insufficient for production APR use.
Twitter data may not generalize to other social media platforms.
